name: Heldai
overview: Heldai is a male figure mentioned in the Bible as one of the exiles who returned from Babylon. Beyond this, Scripture does not provide additional tribal affiliation or further personal details. His mention is brief but significant in the context of the post-exilic restoration period.
namesAndTitles: The name Heldai is a proper name meaning 'mole.' This name does not appear to be given by God and is referenced specifically in Zechariah 6:10. The meaning itself is straightforward and does not carry additional theological significance in the text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Heldai beyond his identification as one of the returned exiles. There are no listed relatives or connections provided in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Heldai's importance lies in his role as one of the returning exiles from Babylon, marking him as part of the community involved in the restoration of Israel after the captivity. His mention in Zechariah 6:10 situates him within the prophetic vision concerning the rebuilding and renewal of Jerusalem under God's providence. Though not extensively detailed, Heldai represents the faithful remnant who returned to their homeland to fulfill God's purposes.
